terra.problem: The elders appear later in Deuteronomy 25, not later in this chapter.
The text says the newlywed must not be pressed into duty. It does not say he may accept no assignments at all.
The text says the millstones are his livelihood. It does not say he cannot earn enough to repay the debt without them.
Numbers 12:10 does not establish that Miriam was Moses' sister. That fact needs a supporting reference.
Numbers 12:10–11 does not establish that Aaron was Moses' brother and Israel's high priest. Those facts need supporting references.
The passage does not say returning the cloak takes a few minutes or costs the lender nothing but a blanket.
The text says the worker is poor and depends on his wages. It does not say he has nothing to spare.
The law says a child is not to be put to death for his father. Saying a son does not pay for his father's sin broadens it beyond that death sentence.
Saying everybody carries only their own sin broadens the law beyond its specific rule about being put to death.
Moses recalls Israel's slavery and redemption, but the text does not say they must show others the same care they were shown.
The pop quiz comparison invokes a school scenario, which is outside the audience rules.
Sunset comes up in Deuteronomy 24, not in this chapter.
The passage instructs the widow to go to the elders at the gate; it does not state the general historical claim that they handled matters like this there.
